title: Compatibility with finite scalar extension
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E\subset E'$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and let $T$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the completed integral coefficient categories and their raw rationalizations $\Dbc(T,E)$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], with no Karoubi envelope. Derived scalar extension means integral change of completed coefficient rings followed by scalar localization. Then it defines an exact functor
$$T_{E'/E}=E'\otimes_E^L-:\Dbc(T,E)\longrightarrow\Dbc(T,E').$$
Choose $T_{E/E}=\operatorname{id}$ literally. For $E\subset E'\subset E''$, balancing of derived tensor specifies an exact natural isomorphism
$$a_{E'',E',E}:T_{E''/E'}T_{E'/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{E''/E}.$$
The associators satisfy the unit equations and the pentagon for four nested fields. There are canonical natural shift comparisons
$$\sigma_{E'/E,K}:T_{E'/E}(K[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(T_{E'/E}K)[1]$$
commuting with these associators.

Write $C_{E'/E,T}(K)=K\otimes^L_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E',T}$ for the integral ambient scalar-extension functor; its constructible restriction and rationalization is $T_{E'/E,T}$. For morphisms $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ between schemes satisfying the same scheme hypotheses, there are coherent comparisons on ambient derived-complete integral categories
$$C_{E'/E,Y}Rf_{*,\mathcal O_E}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{*,\mathcal O_{E'}}C_{E'/E,X},\qquad
C_{E'/E,Y'}Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp},\mathcal O_E}\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp},\mathcal O_{E'}}C_{E'/E,Y}.$$
Their restrictions and rationalizations are comparisons on $\Dbc$ whenever the displayed operations preserve those constructible categories; no preservation assertion for arbitrary $f$ is implicit. Here ordinary direct image is the ringed-topos derived direct image, and completed pullback is [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. For a cartesian square $(f,f',g,g')$ whose four schemes satisfy the stated hypotheses, the exchange is the canonical ambient ringed-topos mate of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange], followed by derived completion and the direct-image/completion comparison, and then rationalization. Under the displayed comparisons, scalar extension of this $E$-exchange is this $E'$-exchange. The comparisons respect identity morphisms, composition, successive coefficient extensions and shifts.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_E$, $B=\mathcal O_{E'}$, $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_{E'}$, $R_T=\widehat A_T$, $S_T=\widehat B_T$. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], $S_T$ is a finite free $R_T$-module and, for derived $t$-complete $K$, $K\otimes^L_{R_T}S_T$ is derived $v$-complete and is canonically the completed integral scalar extension. The local-completeness and intrinsic Koszul-completeness conventions agree by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] to $K\in\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$: on a finite stratification it has local models $R_T\otimes_A^LP$ with $P$ bounded finite projective over $A$. For each stratum inclusion and each pro-etale localization, the completed coefficient sheaves restrict to the corresponding coefficient sheaves: for the scheme inclusion use [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image], and for a slice localization restriction commutes with the defining limits. Tensoring a model with $S_T$ gives $S_T\otimes_B^L(B\otimes_A P)$. Each term of $B\otimes_A P$ is finite projective, since a splitting $P^i\oplus Q^i=A^{r_i}$ remains a splitting after tensoring. The same finite stratification and local termwise bounds therefore give condition (ii) of that characterization over $B$. Its implication (ii) to (i) supplies all the uniform tower and compatible etale-witness requirements of the PBC category. This proves membership without identifying the PBC category with a different coefficient formalism.

source.place: 093M, lemma-completion-flat; local-model argument written by the worker using the cited characterization

proof.text: The ordinary ring-sheaf change of rings $K\mapsto K\otimes^L_{R_T}S_T$ is exact by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. By [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-complete-triangulated] the source and target PBC integral categories have exactly the inherited triangles. Step 1 shows that the exact ambient functor restricts to them. On integral morphisms its $A$-linearity is the identity $(af)\otimes1=a(f\otimes1)$ on tensor representatives. Define the rational functor on morphisms by $f/t^n\mapsto F(f)/t^n$. This is well-defined under the balancing and localization relations in [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. The image of $t$ is invertible in the target rational category: by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], the nonzero nonunit $t\in B$ is $uv^e$ for a unit $u$ and $e\geq1$. Localization at $t$ and at $v$ gives the same morphism modules because $v^{-1}=uv^{e-1}t^{-1}$ and $t^{-1}=u^{-1}v^{-e}$. By [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated], every rational distinguished triangle is isomorphic to a localized integral triangle; its image is consequently distinguished. This proves exactness of the displayed functor on the raw rationalizations. In Lean, the counit-normalized ambient shift is obtained from [lem-pur-right-kan-extension-coherent-shift], and exactness for precisely that shift follows from [lem-sbc-derived-scalar-extension-counit-shift]. Restrict through the fully faithful integral inclusion. Descend the shift along scalar localization and use essential surjectivity on arrows to descend exactness; the localization comparison retains the prescribed shift equation.

source.place: exactness clause; explicit scalar-localization argument written by the worker

proof.text: For three nested coefficient rings $R\to S\to U$, choose a K-flat resolution $P$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Such representatives compute derived change of rings by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]; $P\otimes_R S$ is again K-flat with flat terms by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings]. Define the associator by $((p\otimes s)\otimes u)\mapsto p\otimes su$, with inverse $p\otimes u\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes u$. These maps respect balancing, restrictions and differentials. They are mutually inverse and commute with every chain map of representatives. They hence descend through the derived localizations, and through scalar localization by the formula of step 2. Comparison with completed scalar extension is the natural comparison of step 1; choose these balanced maps as the specified associators for that realization. Replace the identity-extension functor by the literal identity via multiplication $p\otimes r\mapsto rp$. When any two adjacent fields coincide define the associator through this unit identification.

source.place: specified associator and literal identity clauses; balancing calculation written by the worker

proof.text: For four coefficient rings $R\to S\to U\to V$, every route around the associativity pentagon sends $(((p\otimes s)\otimes u)\otimes v)$ to $p\otimes(suv)$. Associativity of ring multiplication makes the results equal; the universal balancing relations give equality of sheaf maps and then of complex maps. With an identity extension, multiplication by $1$ gives the two unit equations. Use the shift comparison which is the identity on $P^{q+1}\otimes_RS$: both differentials are $-d_P\otimes1$. Thus the associator is the same multiplication map in both shifted complexes, proving shift compatibility. Tensoring the cone $Q^q\oplus P^{q+1}$ gives the cone of the tensor map, with the same differential matrix, so these comparisons are comparisons of exact functors. Equalities of these maps persist in the two localizations of step 2.

source.place: unit, pentagon and shift clauses; explicit chain-level calculation written by the worker

proof.text: For a scheme morphism $f$, [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] identifies $f^{-1}R_Y=R_X$ and $f^{-1}S_Y=S_X$, naturally in the coefficient ring maps. For the adic hypotheses, [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] gives Noetherian DVRs $A,B$ with finite residue fields. The quotient $A/t^n$ has $n$ residue-field factors and free resolution $[A\xrightarrow{t^n}A]$, so is finite, perfect and additive torsion; likewise $B/v^n$. Define $\beta_f$ in $D(S_Y)$ by transposing $C_X(\varepsilon^R_{f,K})$ through the balanced pullback comparison $Lf_S^*C_Y\cong C_XLf_R^*$. Its restriction is the projection mate with coefficient object $S_Y$, an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula] since $S_Y$ is finite free (step 1). To identify restriction of the target direct image, use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] for the identity topos and $R_X\to S_X$. For K-injective $J$ over $S_X$ and acyclic $R_X$-complex $H$, maps $H\to\operatorname{Res}J$ identify with maps $H\otimes_{R_X}S_X\to J$. The latter source is acyclic by finite freeness, so its maps are null-homotopic by [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Thus restriction preserves K-injectives; the underived equality $f_*\operatorname{Res}J=\operatorname{Res}f_*J$ computes the derived equality. Restriction detects quasi-isomorphisms because underlying abelian sheaves are unchanged. Hence $\beta_f$ is an isomorphism in $D(S_Y)$. Thus [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] applies separately to $(A,(t))$ and $(B,(v))$: derived complete $K$ has derived complete $Rf_*K$. Its intrinsic Koszul convention agrees with local completeness by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Both endpoints therefore lie in the claimed complete categories.

source.place: 0944, lemma-projection-formula, finite-free case; coefficient-action and K-injective checks written by the worker

proof.text: Ordinary pullback commutes with coefficient extension by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and the coefficient inverse-image identifications of step 5. Now complete this comparison. The completed pullback of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] is ordinary pullback followed by its canonical completion unit. Finite-free tensor commutes with the Koszul completion construction: a basis of $S_{T'}$ over $R_{T'}$ identifies it with a finite sum, finite sums commute with derived products, and the matrix $1-s$ in the functorial strict-tower Roos realization commutes with that finite sum. The canonical map, defined before choosing the basis, is therefore an isomorphism and respects the completion units. The Roos realization is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Completion with respect to $t$ and $v$ in $S_{T'}$ is the same reflector: $t=uv^e$ implies $S[1/t]=S[1/v]$ with the same localization map from $S$. The extended Cech complexes for these single generators are consequently the identical augmented complex $[S\to S[1/v]]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-extended-cech-completion-model], derived Hom from this augmented complex realizes both completion reflectors and their units. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector], the Koszul completion constructions are also these reflectors, so their canonical isomorphism is uniquely fixed by the units. This gives the claimed completed-pullback comparison without claiming that ordinary pullback of an arbitrary complete object is complete. Conversely, once this unit-normalized completion comparison is available, preservation of intrinsic completeness follows formally: the source completion unit is invertible on a complete input, so its tensor image and then the target completion unit are invertible. Transport completeness back from the reflector along that unit.

source.place: 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (2),(5); finite-free completion comparison written by the worker

proof.text: The comparisons just constructed are coherent. For coefficient towers, take successively tensor-product bases of the finite-free extensions. The projection comparison of step 5, after restriction of scalars, is the direct sum of identity maps $Rf_*K\to Rf_*K$ indexed by a basis. This follows from its counit-tensor definition and the tensor-unit case of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Iterating two comparisons or using their associator in step 3 gives the same identities indexed by pairs of basis elements. Changing a basis conjugates both routes by the same scalar matrix, so the resulting equality is independent of the bases. Every arrow compared here has an extended source $CN$ (for a coefficient tower $C_{U/S}C_{S/R}N\cong C_{U/R}N$ by step 3). By [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], $a\mapsto\operatorname{Res}(a)\circ\eta_N$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(S)}(CN,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(N,\operatorname{Res}H)$, so two such arrows that agree after restriction of scalars are equal in the extended-coefficient derived category. Use the canonical composition comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] and [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. For composed scheme morphisms the counit of the composite adjunction is the composite of the two counits; tensoring these with $1$ gives the same direct sums of identities. For pullback these equations are the balanced formula of step 3 on the canonical compositions of inverse images. For completed pullback they persist because the completion isomorphisms in step 6 are uniquely fixed by the completion units. The same equations with a single basis element $1$ give identity coherence. Shift coherence follows from the counit-tensor shift equation in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] and the explicit shift formula in step 4. The formal completed identity equation cancels the target completion unit, applies naturality and the normalization of the scalar/completion comparison, and reduces to ordinary pullback identity coherence. The formal coefficient-composition equation uses naturality of the scalar/completion comparison, its coefficient-composition equation (proved by reflector uniqueness), and ordinary pullback coefficient coherence.

source.place: 0944, lemma-projection-formula, tensor-unit case; coherence calculation written by the worker

proof.text:
Write $\beta_f:C_YRf_{*,R}\to Rf_{*,S}C_X$ for step 5 and $\delta_u:Lu_S^*C_V\cong C_ULu_R^*$ for the ordinary pullback comparison. In $D(S_X)$ its defining transpose says
$$\varepsilon^S_f\,Lf_S^*\beta_f=C_X\varepsilon^R_f\,\delta_f.$$
The two routes comparing $C_{Y'}Lg_R^*Rf_{*,R}K$ with $Rf'_{*,S}Lg_S'^*C_XK$ are equal: transpose each under $Lf_S'^*\dashv Rf'_{*,S}$ and insert this defining equation for $\beta_f$ and $\beta_{f'}$. Both transposes become $C_{X'}(Lg_R'^*\varepsilon^R_f\circ\theta^R_{\square,Rf_{*,R}K})$, precomposed with the same $\delta_{f'}$ and $\delta_g$ identifications. The identifications agree because both balanced coefficient maps send $p\otimes s$ to $p\otimes s$ through the equality $fg'=gf'$. The adjunction bijection of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] gives equality in $D(S_{Y'})$. The exchange being transposed is exactly [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. This is also the projection/exchange identity of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] with $Q=S_Y$, now verified before forgetting the $S$-module structure.

proof.text:
For any edge $f$ and any ambient $M$, let $\gamma^R_f:\Lambda_R Rf_{*,R}M\cong Rf_{*,R}\Lambda_R M$ and $\gamma^S_f$ be the unit-normalized comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pushforward-completion]. Let $\kappa:C\Lambda_R\cong\Lambda_S C$ be step 6, using the image of $t$ for both completions. Then
$$\beta_{f,\Lambda_R M}\,C\gamma^R_{f,M}
=Rf_{*,S}(\kappa_M^{-1})\,\gamma^S_{f,CM}\,\Lambda_S(\beta_{f,M})\,\kappa_{Rf_{*,R}M}.$$
Indeed precompose both sides with $C\eta^R_{Rf_{*,R}M}$. The defining unit equations for $\gamma$ and $\kappa$ reduce the first side to $\beta_{f,\Lambda_R M}\,C Rf_{*,R}\eta^R_M$, and the second to $Rf_{*,S}(C\eta^R_M)\,\beta_{f,M}$; these are equal by naturality of $\beta_f$. The source is the completion of $C Rf_{*,R}M$ and the common target is complete. The reflector bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] therefore proves the displayed equality. This is the compatibility with the specified direct-image/completion comparison. Its specialization to $Rf'_*Lg'^*K$ completes the ambient exchange equality in step 8, with precisely the completed pullback comparison in step 6. The $t$- and $v$-reflectors and their units were identified there, so this also proves the equality with the stated $v$-completed exchange.

proof.text: Restrict all these arrows whenever the displayed operations preserve the integral constructible categories. By [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] their exact linear functors and specified natural transformations extend to raw rationalizations. For coefficient change, use the denominator formula and $t=uv^e$ of step 2. Every equality above is already an equality on integral components, hence remains that equality on fractions. This gives the claimed comparisons and exchange compatibility on $\Dbc$, with the identity, composition, coefficient-tower and shift coherence proved in steps 3, 4 and 7.

tool_uses.why: Steps 1 and 3 use finite freeness of the completed coefficient sheaf and its canonical comparison with completed scalar extension. The torsion proper-base-change unit does not construct change of completed coefficient rings.

Steps 2 and 3 use exact unbounded derived ring-sheaf change of rings and its computation on K-flat resolutions. This is generic ringed-site algebra, not a replacement of the unit's torsion proper-base-change proof.

Step 3 uses preservation of K-flatness and termwise flatness under ring-sheaf change of rings to compute successive extensions on one representative. The proper-base-change unit does not supply this resolving-class theorem.

Step 2 uses the valuation-ring factorization t = u v^e to compare scalar localizations under ramification; step 5 uses the Noetherian DVR and finite residue field to verify finite perfect torsion quotients. The torsion proper-base-change unit does not prove this coefficient valuation-ring structure.

Step 2 uses the characterization of rational distinguished triangles as localized integral triangles. This general linear triangulated-category construction is not furnished by the proper-base-change unit's three torsion steps.

Step 3 uses existence of K-flat resolutions with flat terms on an arbitrary ringed site to compute successive changes of rings on one representative. This generic resolution theorem is not furnished by the proper-base-change unit.

Step 7 uses the derived change-of-rings/restriction adjunction to conclude equality in the extended-coefficient derived category from equality after restriction, for arrows out of extended objects. Generic ringed-site algebra, not a replacement of the unit's torsion PBC route.

For a finite extension $E\subset E'$, derived scalar extension is an exact
functor
$$
 T_{E'/E}=E'\otimes_E^L-:
 \Dbc(T,E)\longrightarrow\Dbc(T,E').
$$
Choose $T_{E/E}=\operatorname{id}$ literally. For $E\subset E'\subset E''$,
derived tensor associativity gives a specified exact natural isomorphism
$$
 a_{E'',E',E}:T_{E''/E'}T_{E'/E}
 \xrightarrow{\sim}T_{E''/E}.
$$
These associators satisfy the unit equations and the pentagon for four
nested fields. Exactness supplies natural shift comparisons
$$
 \sigma_{E'/E,K}:T_{E'/E}(K[1])
 \xrightarrow{\sim}(T_{E'/E}K)[1]
$$
which commute with the associators.

There are coherent natural isomorphisms
$$
 E'\otimes_E^LRf_{*,E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}
 Rf_{*,E'}(E'\otimes_E^LK)
$$
and analogous isomorphisms for pullback. Under these isomorphisms, scalar
extension of the $E$-exchange map is the $E'$-exchange map.
